options.text: The breaking apart of molecules by chemical reactions
The absorption of radiation by a stable nucleus
The spontaneous emission of radiation from an unstable nucleus
The loss of electrons from an atom

questions.explanation: Radioactive decay is the spontaneous emission of radiation (alpha, beta, or gamma) from an unstable nucleus as it changes to become more stable. It is random and cannot be controlled.

options.text: A neutron emitted from the nucleus
A helium nucleus (2 protons and 2 neutrons)

questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus consisting of 2 protons and 2 neutrons. It has a charge of +2 and a mass number of 4, making it the largest and most ionising type of nuclear radiation.

questions.stem: Which type of radiation has the greatest penetrating power?

options.text: All three have equal penetrating power

questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the greatest penetrating power. They can pass through most materials and are only significantly reduced by thick lead or several metres of concrete. Alpha is stopped by paper, and beta by a few millimetres of aluminium.

questions.stem: Which two properties of radioactive decay make it impossible to predict when a specific nucleus will decay?
questions.explanation: Radioactive decay is random (we cannot predict which nucleus will decay next) and spontaneous (it happens without any external trigger and is unaffected by temperature, pressure, or chemical conditions).

questions.stem: Which type of radiation is the most ionising?
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are the most ionising because they are large, heavy, and strongly charged (+2). They interact strongly with atoms they pass, stripping electrons and creating many ions over a short distance.

options.text: A high-speed electron emitted from the nucleus when a neutron turns into a proton
A proton emitted from the nucleus

questions.explanation: A beta particle is a high-speed electron emitted from the nucleus. It is created when a neutron changes into a proton, and the electron is ejected. It has a charge of -1 and negligible mass.

questions.stem: What can be used to detect radioactive emissions?
questions.explanation: A Geiger-Muller (GM) tube connected to a counter is used to detect and measure radioactive emissions. The tube detects ionising radiation and the counter records the count rate.
